raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Motivation

Qwen-Image 2.1's QwenImage21Attention projects Q/K/V from one activation with three separate [C, C] linears. convrot_int8 has two kernel backends:

  • the JIT / customkernel backend (CC 9.0 / 10.0 / 12.0 / 12.1), which #38040 already gives a fused single rotation + activation quantisation for q/k/v sharing one input;

  • the comfy_kitchen backend, which serves the GPUs the JIT ops do not build for (CC 8.x Ampere/Ada, CC 10.3) and has no equivalent: every attention block pays two redundant ConvRot activation quantisations and issues three narrow GEMMs.

On a GPU with no FP8/NVFP4 tensor cores -- A100 (CC 8.0), RTX 30/40-series -- the comfy_kitchen backend is not a fallback, it is the only INT8 path, so this gap is real there.

Modifications

  1. layers/quantization/convrot_int8_comfy_kitchen.py: the fused kernel apply ran inline moves to a module-level int8_linear(x, weight, weight_scale, group_size, bias=None, split_out_features=None), and apply becomes a thin adapter. This is a pure refactor: the op, its argument order and its numerics are unchanged, and there is now a single place for the row-split cap. split_out_features lets a packed caller judge the row-split heuristic on the per-projection width instead of the packed width.

  2. models/dits/qwen_image21.py: teach the existing bf16 packing to also cover convrot_int8. The three int8 [C, C] weights and the matching [C, 1] fp32 row scales are re-homed onto one [3C, C] / [3C, 1] storage each, and _project_qkv_packed_convrot_int8 projects all three through a single int8_linear call. A new BitExactFusionGate verifies the first call against the module forwards and falls back on any mismatch, so the packed path can only ever be used when it is bit-exact.

  3. test/unit/test_qwen_image21.py: four new unit tests -- storage sharing keeps values and shares one storage; the packing predicate requires the convrot_int8 method; the consecutive-slice view rejects gaps and separate storages; the packed int8_linear call is bit-exact against the separate per-projection calls at production shapes.

Accuracy Tests

Packed call is bit-exact against the separate calls (max_abs = 0.0); cat(quantize(W_i)) equals quantize(cat(W_i)) exactly. End-to-end on A100 GPU 0 (1024x1024, 40 steps, CFG 1, seed 42), the output PNG md5 is identical to the frozen INT8 baseline: 05288a62012b1353230d53c3297cb67c. The whole flow is inside the existing bit-exact gate, so an unexpected mismatch disables the fusion rather than changing the output.

Speed Tests and Profiling

A100 GPU 0 (CC 8.0, comfy_kitchen backend), Qwen-Image 2.1, 1024x1024 @ 40 steps, CFG 1:

arm | denoise | per step | output md5 -- | -- | -- | -- convrot_int8, unpacked QKV | 9.059 s | -- | 05288a62... convrot_int8, packed QKV (this PR) | 8.796 s | 0.220 s | 05288a62...

Kernel level (M=4114, C=4096, group_size=256): 1.263 ms -> 1.005 ms per attention block (-0.257 ms/block, -8.2 ms/step); the whole saving is the removed ConvRot work.

Scope: on JIT-capable GPUs (H100/H200/Blackwell) the equivalent fusion already exists via the customkernel backend, so this PR is a backend-parity change with no effect there.

Checklist

  • Format your code according to the pre-commit guide.

  • Add unit tests.

  • Update documentation / docstrings as needed.

  • Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.

@@ -59,6 +59,65 @@ def _row_split(rows: int, out_features: int) -> int | None:
     return _MAX_ROWS_PER_CALL
 
 
+def int8_linear(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    weight_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    group_size: int,
+    bias: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    split_out_features: int | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """One fused ConvRot + IMMA GEMM over ``[..., K]`` activations and a 2-D weight.
+
+    ConvRot quantises the activation row-wise, independently of the output
+    columns, so ``weight`` may be a packed ``[sum(N_i), K]`` whose row blocks are
+    several projections of one activation: the call is then bit-exact against
+    one call per projection and drops ``n - 1`` redundant activation
+    quantisations. ``weight_scale`` is the matching ``[sum(N_i), 1]`` scale and
+    ``group_size`` the ConvRot group that every block shares.
+
+    ``split_out_features`` overrides the width the row-split heuristic judges:
+    a packed caller passes the per-projection width so the fused call issues
+    exactly the split the separate calls would have.
+    """
+    out_code = _OUT_DTYPE_CODE.get(x.dtype)
+    if out_code is None:
+        raise ValueError(f"convrot_int8 does not support activation dtype {x.dtype}")
+
+    # The kernel takes 2D activations; callers may pass [..., K].
+    orig_shape = x.shape
+    if x.dim() != 2:
+        x = x.reshape(-1, orig_shape[-1])
+    x = x.contiguous()
+
+    def run(rows: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return torch.ops.comfy_kitchen.int8_linear(
+            rows,
+            weight,
+            weight_scale,
+            bias,
+            out_code,
+            True,  # convrot
+            group_size,
+        )
+
+    n_rows, n_out = x.shape[0], weight.shape[0]
+    width = split_out_features if split_out_features is not None else n_out
+    split = _row_split(n_rows, width)
+    if split is None:
+        out = run(x)
+    else:
+        # Row slices of a contiguous 2D tensor are themselves contiguous, so
+        # this splits without copying the activation.
+        out = torch.empty(n_rows, n_out, dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
+        for start in range(0, n_rows, split):
+            out[start : start + split] = run(x[start : start + split])
+
+    if len(orig_shape) != 2:
+        out = out.reshape(*orig_shape[:-1], out.shape[-1])
+    return out
+
+

     """Whether comfy_kitchen is importable and registers int8_linear."""

+        and layer.bias is None

+    """
+    from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.quantization.convrot_int8_comfy_kitchen import (
+        ConvRotInt8ComfyKitchenLinearMethod,

+    scale = getattr(layer, "weight_scale", None)
+    return (
+        type(layer) is ColumnParallelLinear
+        and isinstance(layer.quant_method, ConvRotInt8ComfyKitchenLinearMethod)
+        and layer.bias is None

+def can_pack_convrot_int8_qkv(layers):

+
+    A single fused call takes exactly one group size, so projections with
+    different group sizes cannot share a packed weight.

+    return (

+
+def share_slices(layers, names, rows):
+    """Re-home each attribute on ``layers`` onto one cat'ed [n * rows, ...] storage.
+
+    The parameters keep their names, shapes and values; only their storage
+    moves. No reference to the shared storage is kept, so offloading the
+    parameters still frees it.
+    """
+    for name in names:
+        packed = torch.cat([getattr(layer, name).data for layer in layers], dim=0)
+        for index, layer in enumerate(layers):
+            getattr(layer, name).data = packed[index * rows : (index + 1) * rows]

+
+def consecutive_slices_view(tensors):
+    """``[n * rows, ...]`` view over equal-shaped consecutive slices of one storage, else None.
+
+    No reference to the storage is kept, so offloading the parameters still
+    frees it.
+    """
+    first = tensors[0]

+        t.is_cuda
+        and t.is_contiguous()
+        and t.shape == first.shape
+        and t.dtype is first.dtype
+        for t in tensors
+    ):
+        return None
+    base = first.untyped_storage().data_ptr()
+    stride = first.numel()
+    if not (
+        all(t.untyped_storage().data_ptr() == base for t in tensors)
+        and all(
+            t.storage_offset() == first.storage_offset() + index * stride
+            for index, t in enumerate(tensors)
+        )
+    ):
+        return None
+    return first.as_strided(
+        (len(tensors) * first.shape[0], *first.shape[1:]), first.stride()
+    )
+

+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA required")
+def test_int8_linear_packed_weight_is_bit_exact_against_separate_calls():
+    pytest.importorskip("comfy_kitchen")
+    from comfy_kitchen.tensor.int8 import TensorWiseINT8Layout
+
+    from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.quantization.convrot_int8_comfy_kitchen import (
+        int8_linear,
+    )
+
+    def quantize(w):
+        qdata, params = TensorWiseINT8Layout.quantize(
+            w,
+            is_weight=True,
+            per_channel=True,
+            convrot=True,
+            convrot_groupsize=256,
+            stochastic_rounding=0,
+        )
+        return qdata.contiguous(), params.scale.to(torch.float32).contiguous()
+
+    # Production shapes (C=4096, M=4096): at these the packed [3C, C] call and
+    # the separate [C, C] calls share one CUTLASS tile schedule, so the call is
+    # bit-exact (mirrors the 20261013-1610 bench and the e2e md5 check).
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    c = 4096
+    m = 4096
+    weights = torch.randn(3 * c, c, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    x = torch.randn(m, c, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    q_full, scale_full = quantize(weights)
+    packed = int8_linear(x, q_full, scale_full, 256, split_out_features=c)
+    for i in range(3):
+        q_i, scale_i = quantize(weights[i * c : (i + 1) * c])
+        # Quantising the packed weight equals quantising each block, so the
+        # packed storage is exact.
+        assert torch.equal(q_i, q_full[i * c : (i + 1) * c])
+        assert torch.equal(scale_i, scale_full[i * c : (i + 1) * c])
+        # One packed call is bit-exact against the separate calls.
+        assert torch.equal(
+            packed[:, i * c : (i + 1) * c],
+            int8_linear(x, q_i, scale_i, 256),
+        )
